item.title: Ready To Feel Old? The Switch 1 Reveal Trailer Launched A Whopping 10 Years Ago Today

description.p: Ha Ha Ha Ha (nope).We're all mature enough that we understand the concept of time. Yes, today, 20th October 2026, marks a whopping 10 years since Nintendo introduced the world to the system we now lovingly call the 'Switch 1'.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Talking Point: How Did You First Encounter Zelda: Ocarina Of Time?

description.p: Fairy Tales.In case you haven't noticed, another chance to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is on the horizon. The coming 5th November release date for the Switch 2 remake has got us diving into our OoT memory banks and feeling all nostalgic about where our love for the game began — after all, you can replay it as many times as you like, but you only get a 'first playthrough' once.For most of us here at Nintendo Life Towers, those early memories take us back to the N64, though some people will have first encountered the game through the GameCube, its 3DS remake or the NSO library. Heck, you might not have even heard of this little-known curio until Nintendo announced it for Switch 2 (we doubt that will be many of you reading this, but hey, there's a chance).Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Nintendo "Underestimated" Zelda Switch 2 Console Sales, But Promises Restocks Are On The Way

description.p: "Please be patient".If you are anything like us, the reveal of the special edition Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 console last month was quickly followed by the dreaded realisation of "oh no, I need this". Alas, for many, this need has not been fulfilled, with supply shortages making those all-important pre-orders far rarer than we'd like them to be.In a recent interview with YouTube channel Coelho no Japão, Nintendo's Latin America Vice President and General Manager Bill van Zyll admitted that the company had "underestimated" the demand for the console, and reaffirmed that further restocks are on the way (thanks for the heads up, GamesRadar+).Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Feature: The Seven-Year Silence: How Ocarina Of Time Held My Grief At Seven Years Old

description.p: A safe space to process the unthinkable.The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is frequently crowned the greatest game ever made, celebrated for its dungeons, its music, and a critical legacy that stands as the highest-reviewed title in gaming history. For those of us who were there at the time, it was for gaming what the sequence in The Wizard of Oz is when the world around Dorothy turns to colour: pure magic and wonder.But for those of us who look to art to make sense of the unthinkable, it was something much more fragile and vital. In the summer of my seventh year my world collapsed, and that same winter a Nintendo 64 cartridge became the only safe space I had left to process the loss of my father.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Slim Or Fuller? Atelier Karia "Body Shape Change Feature" Confirmed

description.p: "What kind of Karia would you like to adventure with?".The Koei Tecmo fantasy alchemy RPG Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of Memories is making its way to the Switch 2 early next year. In an update from Gust this week, it confirmed a "body shape change feature" is officially on the way.In a post on the game's website, the developer revealed it has decided to implement this feature based on recent community survey results and feedback. Karia's body shape "will change depending on how much she eats during snacks". Players will also be able to turn the body shape changes "on" and "off" (and lock the shape) based on their preferences.Read the full article on nintendolife.com
